longest_story.title: Dick Grayson, Author!
longest_story.first_line: Did you ever stop to wonder exactly what makes a Batman story?

longest_story.synopsis: Dick, interested in comic magazines, accompanies Bruce to the offices of the editor of Crescent Comics, and is invited to write a script. However, ideas do not come easy and is superseded by a case involving ex-con Big Ed Conroy. The Dick discovers that he can use real facts for his story, which is soon published and titled "Crooks' Come-Back".
longest_story.notes:
We originally credited this story to Sprang alone.

Craig Delich changed those credits to Sprang (layouts), Bob Kane (pencils), and Burnley (inks), saying "There are a few indications that display partial art by Sprang, especially panels 3 and 4 on page 12 (that is Sprang's bat on Batman's chest, not Kane's), and throughout the story, there is no cape knot at Batman's throat (such as seen in the previous two stories by Kane and Burnley). The Robin figures on the splash and first two pages appear to be Sprang's work (as is the cover), and maybe a few other random Robins." In addition, Kane told Joe Desris that these stories were his pencils with Burnley inking him.

However, Martin O'Hearn has identified the penciler as Cooper, not Bob Kane.
longest_story.keywords: Crescent Comics; Gotham City; Security Messenger Service; State Prison; Wayne Mansion

longest_story.synopsis: The Penguin opens a new restaurant in town, but queerly asks guests to hand-write their orders and sign them, then he does everything possible to get himself arrested. longest_story.title: The Origin of the Batman!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne] (origin retold in detail); Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Thomas Wayne (flashback, death); Martha Wayne (flashback, death); Joe Chill (villain, name revealed in this story, Thomas and Martha Wayne's murderer, death); Feets Borgam (killer, death); Monty Julep (illegal gambler, death)
longest_story.synopsis: While investigating criminal activity at a transport company, Batman recognizes the owner, Joe Chill, as the man who killed Thomas and Martha Wayne years before.  Batman tries to find evidence of  Chill's illegal operations, but when he fails, he decides to reveal his identity to Chill and tells him that will be watching him and will catch him eventually.  In a panic, Chill flees to his gang, but when they find out Chill is responsible for Batman's existence they shoot him, and only after do they realize that they should have asked Chill for Batman's real name.
